newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Jobs seen sticking point in Fokker talks.
newsitem.headline: Jobs seen sticking point in Fokker talks.

text.p: Talks between South Korea's Samsung Aerospace and the Dutch government on the revival of bankrupt plane-maker Fokker NV were foundering on the issue of job security, Dutch media reported on Wednesday.
Newspaper De Volkskrant said the negotiations were at a difficult stage as the company did not want to meet the government's demand that jobs be guaranteed for 10 years.
"There should be complete clarity as this is a breaking point for us," the newspaper quoted Wim Van Gelder, a member of the coalition government's socialist party member the PvdA, as saying.

Samsung, which has been given an exclusive look at Fokker's books, has proposed that the government take a minority stake in, and provide large subsidies to, the loss-making company, which collapsed in March after German parent Daimler Benz Aerospace cut credit lines.
Dutch newsagency ANP quoted van Gelder as saying: "We are only willing to invest if there are guarantees. There are not sufficient guarantees (now)."
Van Gelder was speaking on Tuesday after a closed meeting of the Dutch parliament's Economic Aaffairs committee involving Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers.
De Volkskrant said Wijers wanted Samsung to maintain Fokker's current aircraft construction activities and also develop a new plane in the Netherlands in the longer run.
A spokesman for the Economic Affairs ministry could not be contacted.
